headline.purpose: The page title, and the only element at this size. Always tracking-tight. One per page.

title.purpose: Section and card headings. The step down from headline is deliberately large; there is no 20px rung in normal use.

body.purpose: The working size. Table cells, form values, descriptions, and nearly everything the operator reads.

label.purpose: Metadata, timestamps, status badge text, helper copy, column headers. Sentence case, never uppercase.

mono.purpose: Identifiers where character alignment beats reading rhythm: revision hashes, FG-{number} codes, quantities.

shadows.name: hairline-ring
shadows.purpose: The only in-page depth device. Applied to cards as a ring rather than a border, so it sits outside the box model and never shifts layout.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Focus-visible on every interactive primitive. Thick on purpose: at 32px control height a 1px outline is invisible against a dense table.

shadows.name: focus-ring-inline
shadows.purpose: The established exception, used on bare inline links inside prose rather than on primitives.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Reserved for things that genuinely float above the page and will be dismissed: dialog, popover, sheet, toast, the revealed skip link. Never on an in-page surface.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: The system's one piece of physical feedback, on button :active. Suppressed on menu triggers so a popover anchor does not shift under an opening panel.

motion.name: sidebar-collapse
motion.purpose: Width transition when the navigation rail collapses to icons.

motion.name: state-color
motion.purpose: The entire motion vocabulary available to a feature template. Hover and state colour shifts only; no page-level or entrance choreography.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single committed action on a screen. A page with two has not decided what it wants the operator to do.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.375rem; height: 2rem; padding: 0 0.625rem; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: var(--radius, 0.625rem); font-family: 'Geist Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; user-select: none; outline: none; transition: all 150ms ease; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn:focus-visible { border-color: var(--ring); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring) 50%, transparent); } .ds-btn-default { background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-foreground); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: The workhorse secondary: page ground with a hairline border, hovering to Wash.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.375rem; height: 2rem; padding: 0 0.625rem; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: var(--radius, 0.625rem); font-family: 'Geist Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; user-select: none; outline: none; transition: all 150ms ease; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn:focus-visible { border-color: var(--ring); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring) 50%, transparent); } .ds-btn-outline { background: var(--background); color: var(--foreground); border-color: var(--border); } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: var(--muted); }

components.name: Destructive Button
components.description: Tinted ground with coloured text, never a solid red fill. A filled red button reads as the page's primary action, which a delete never is.

components.name: Status Badge — Urgent
components.description: The signature component the whole colour system exists to serve. Transparent ground, hairline border, muted label; only the 12px glyph carries tone. The double chevron encodes rank by shape, so the scale survives greyscale.
components.html: Urgent
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.25rem; width: fit-content; height: 1.25rem; padding: 0.125rem 0.375rem; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 1.625rem; background: transparent; color: var(--muted-foreground); font-family: 'Geist Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; } .ds-badge-icon { flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-glyph-danger { color: oklch(63.7% 0.237 25.331); }

components.name: Status Badge — Published
components.description: The positive terminal state. Only the two ends of a workflow enumeration carry colour; every intermediate step renders the same badge with a neutral grey glyph.
components.html: Published
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.25rem; width: fit-content; height: 1.25rem; padding: 0.125rem 0.375rem; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 1.625rem; background: transparent; color: var(--muted-foreground); font-family: 'Geist Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; } .ds-badge-icon { flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-glyph-success { color: oklch(72.3% 0.219 149.579); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Transparent well with a hairline stroke. 16px text below md is not a style choice: it is what stops iOS Safari zooming the viewport on focus.
components.html: <input class="ds-input" type="text" placeholder="Search interventions" aria-label="Search interventions" />
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; min-width: 0; height: 2rem; padding: 0.25rem 0.625rem; border: 1px solid var(--input); border-radius: var(--radius, 0.625rem); background: transparent; color: var(--foreground); font-family: 'Geist Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; outline: none; transition: color 150ms ease, border-color 150ms ease, box-shadow 150ms ease; } @media (min-width: 768px) { .ds-input { font-size: 0.875rem; } } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--muted-foreground); } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color: var(--ring); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring) 50%, transparent); } .ds-input[aria-invalid='true'] { border-color: var(--destructive); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, var(--destructive) 20%, transparent); } .ds-input:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--input) 50%, transparent); }

components.name: Card
components.description: A hairline ring rather than a border or a shadow, so it sits outside the box model and never doubles up against an adjacent divider.
components.html:
Next recommended action

Assign a responsible agent before planning this intervention.
components.css: .ds-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1rem; padding: 1rem; border-radius: 0.875rem; background: var(--card); color: var(--card-foreground); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in oklab, var(--foreground) 10%, transparent); overflow: hidden; font-family: 'Geist Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; } .ds-card-title { margin: 0; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 600; } .ds-card-body { margin: 0; color: var(--muted-foreground); }

components.name: Sidebar Nav Item
components.description: Ghost-styled rows with no border and no ground at rest, so the navigation column reads as a list rather than a stack of buttons.
components.html: Interventions
components.css: .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; width: 100%; height: 2rem; padding: 0 0.5rem; border-radius: 0.5rem; background: transparent; color: var(--sidebar-foreground); font-family: 'Geist Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; text-decoration: none; outline: none; transition: background 150ms ease, color 150ms ease; } .ds-nav-item svg { flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: var(--sidebar-accent); color: var(--sidebar-accent-foreground); } .ds-nav-item[aria-current='page'] { background: var(--sidebar-accent); color: var(--sidebar-accent-foreground); font-weight: 600; } .ds-nav-item:focus-visible { box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, var(--sidebar-ring) 50%, transparent); }

components.name: Empty State
components.description: A dashed border marks a container with nothing in it yet. Three inputs stand in for a six-element composition, so thirteen call sites cannot get it wrong thirteen different ways.
components.html:
No interventions yet

Interventions you plan will appear here.
components.css: .ds-empty { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; text-align: center; gap: 0.5rem; padding: 2.5rem; border: 1px dashed var(--border); border-radius: 0.5rem; font-family: 'Geist Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-empty-media { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 2.5rem; height: 2.5rem; margin-bottom: 0.25rem; border-radius: 0.5rem; background: var(--muted); color: var(--muted-foreground); } .ds-empty-title { margin: 0; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--foreground); } .ds-empty-description { margin: 0; font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--muted-foreground); }

narrative.overview:
FireGuard is an operator's console. It is dense, unambiguous, and built for someone who already knows what they are doing and needs zero friction between intent and action. Nothing on screen is there to impress: every pixel is either a value to read, a control to press, or the whitespace that keeps the two apart. The interface is the flat panel a professional works against for eight hours, not a page they visit.

The system is achromatic by decision. Surfaces, text, borders and controls are pure zero-chroma neutral — genuinely neither warm nor cool. Colour is not a decorative resource here; it is a scarce, load-bearing signal, and it is spent in exactly one place: the glyph of a status indicator. That single constraint is what makes a dense table readable. When nothing else is coloured, a red chevron at 12px is impossible to miss.

Density is the second half of the identity. The largest type in the entire application is 24px, and 86% of sized text is 14px or 12px. Controls are 32px tall. This is deliberate compression: more of the operator's actual work fits in one viewport, and the interface stops competing with the data it carries.
keyCharacteristics: Achromatic neutral palette; chroma confined to status glyphs
Compressed scale — a hard 24px type ceiling, 32px controls
Flat in-page surfaces; a hairline ring instead of shadows or borders
Compact and mechanical controls with a 1px press displacement
Motion belongs to primitives, never to page composition

rules.name: The Glyph Rule
rules.body: Chroma appears on a status icon and nowhere else. The badge around it stays outline — transparent ground, hairline border, muted text — and only the glyph carries tone. Filling the badge instead turns a dense table into a row of coloured pills and destroys the one signal that should stand out.

rules.name: The Two Ends Rule
rules.body: In a workflow enumeration, only the terminal states carry colour: success for the positive end, danger for the destructive one. Every intermediate step is neutral. Colour therefore reads as "this is finished", not as a heat map of progress.

rules.name: The Tint, Never Fill Rule
rules.body: Destructive actions are a 10% destructive ground with destructive text — never a solid red fill. A filled red button reads as the page's primary action, which a delete never is.

rules.name: The 24px Ceiling
rules.body: Nothing in the application renders larger than 1.5rem. There is no display size and no hero type. A screen that needs more presence earns it through spacing and position, not through scale.

rules.name: The One Title Rule
rules.body: A page carries exactly one headline. Sections step straight down to title (1rem); a second 24px heading on the same screen means the page is really two pages.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Labels are sentence case. Uppercase with widened tracking is not part of this system — it appears three times in the entire feature tree and should not spread.

rules.name: The Independent Columns Rule
rules.body: The page never scrolls. Each column owns its own overflow, so the shell, the content and any side panel keep their positions relative to each other no matter how long the content runs.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: In-page depth is a 1px ring at 10% foreground. If a surface needs to separate further, change its tone — do not add a shadow.

rules.name: The Overlay-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this is floating above the page and will be dismissed". Four shadow utilities exist across the entire feature and layout tree; that number should not grow.

rules.name: The Dashed-Means-Absent Rule
rules.body: A dashed border marks a container with nothing in it yet — an empty collection, an unfilled slot, a drop target. Solid means real content. A dashed border never decorates a populated surface, and its destructive variant (40% opacity) marks a slot whose content failed rather than one that was never filled.

dos: Do spend colour only on a status glyph. If a new surface needs to distinguish states, reach for icon, weight, position and tone first.
Do pair every severity colour with a label and an icon, and give the icon aria-hidden so the label is the accessible name.
Do keep a page's largest text at 1.5rem, font-semibold, tracking-tight — the canonical page title is one exact class string, and reusing it verbatim is how the ceiling stays intact.
Do separate in-page surfaces with ring-1 at 10% foreground, or with one tonal step to Wash.
Do use the 32px control height as the default rhythm; step to 24px or 28px inside dense toolbars rather than shrinking padding on a 32px control.
Do give every interactive element a visible 3px focus ring; on bare inline links a 2px ring is the established exception.
Do mark genuinely empty containers with a dashed border.
Do verify every new surface in both themes — dark is not a filter, it inverts the primary relationship and makes borders translucent.
donts: Don't reintroduce a chromatic brand accent. The interface is achromatic by decision; indigo lives on the mark and in browser chrome only.
Don't fill a status badge with its severity colour, and don't colour the label. The ground stays transparent and the text stays muted.
Don't colour intermediate workflow states. Only the two terminal ends carry tone.
Don't render a destructive action as a solid red button. Tint the ground and colour the text.
Don't introduce type above 1.5rem, or a display typeface. There is one family at four sizes.
Don't set uppercase with widened tracking as a section eyebrow.
Don't add a shadow to an in-page surface. Shadow means "floating and dismissable".
Don't wrap every section in an identical bordered card. Vary surface levels — borderless headers, carded work surfaces, divider lists — so hierarchy comes from rhythm rather than from boxes.
Don't add page-level motion. Transitions belong to the primitives; a feature template's motion vocabulary is transition-colors and the button's 1px press.
Don't let the page scroll as a whole. Columns own their own overflow.
